template.description: Start a polished GitHub profile README in one click: Profilescape cards, refreshed daily by a GitHub Action.

actions.name: Profilescape - GitHub Profile Cards
actions.description: Self-hosted GitHub profile README cards: 3D contribution graph, stats, top languages, repo cards. Your token, no servers.
actions.about: Profilescape renders a matching set of SVG cards for your GitHub profile README: a 3D contribution landscape, an activity overview, top languages weighted by your real commits, repository cards, a hero banner, tech stack, social badges and an animated contribution grid. It runs inside your own workflow with your own token, so there are no rate limits, no third-party servers and no data leaving GitHub.

actions.name: Profilescape 3D Contribution Graph
actions.description: Turn your GitHub contribution calendar into an animated 3D isometric landscape SVG for your profile README.
actions.about: Your contribution calendar, rebuilt as an isometric 3D landscape: every column is a day, and its height and colour grow with the work you shipped. The card is rendered from your full contribution history with your own token, ships in dark and light variants that follow the viewer's GitHub theme, and rises in with a subtle CSS animation that respects reduced-motion settings.

actions.name: Profilescape Stats Card
actions.description: A clean GitHub stats card for your profile README: contributions, commits, pull requests, streaks and more.
actions.about: A self-hosted alternative to hosted stats cards: one crisp SVG that summarises your last twelve months on GitHub, from contributions and commits to pull requests, reviews and streaks. Numbers come straight from the GitHub GraphQL API with your own token, so private contributions can be included and you never hit a shared rate limit.

actions.name: Profilescape Top Languages Card
actions.description: Top languages card for your GitHub profile README, weighted by your real commits, not just repository bytes.
actions.about: Most language cards count bytes, so one vendored library or generated file can dominate. Profilescape weights each repository's languages by the commits you actually made there over the last year, uses GitHub's official language colours, and lets you hide anything you do not want to show.

actions.name: Profilescape Repo Cards
actions.description: Beautiful, self-updating repository cards for your GitHub profile README: stars, forks, languages and releases.
actions.about: Showcase the projects that matter with repository cards that stay current on their own: description, stars, forks, primary languages and the latest release, rendered as crisp SVGs that link straight to each repository. Pick repositories explicitly or let Profilescape use your pinned and most-starred work.

actions.name: Profilescape Hero Banner
actions.description: Animated hero banner, tech stack and social badges for your GitHub profile README, refreshed by a GitHub Action.
actions.about: Open your profile with a polished hero banner built from your GitHub profile, follow it with a tech stack strip and finish with social badges, all in one consistent theme. Everything is plain SVG generated in your own workflow, with dark and light variants that switch automatically with the viewer's theme.

actions.name: Profilescape Contribution Grid
actions.description: Animated GitHub contribution grid SVG for your profile README, themed to match and rendered with your own token.
actions.about: The familiar contribution heatmap, redrawn with a smooth CSS animation and coloured by your chosen theme instead of the default greens. It is generated from your own contribution calendar with your own token, so it works for private contributions too, and it falls back to a fully drawn static frame for viewers who prefer reduced motion.
